$comment: Quasnooze's capability inventory. Every entry claims evidence — a file or symbol a reader can open. scripts/market.js refuses to credit a capability it cannot prove, and refuses to propose one marked out-of-scope however unanimous the market is. Update this file when a capability lands or dies; a stale inventory makes every comparison wrong in the flattering direction.
$policy: in-scope may be proposed. settled has been decided and is only shown so the decision stays visible. out-of-scope contradicts the product identity in .github/prompts/self-improvement.md; the researcher reports it and the proposer is forbidden from acting on it.

capabilities.name: Read-only commands run without a prompt; anything that changes state still asks
evidence: src/risk.js: classifyCommand -> read / act / blocked
src/agent.js: tier checked before the approval gate; blocked refuses without asking
test/risk.test.js: 10 attack vectors + the agent loop and the QUASNOOZE_RISK_TIERS=0 kill switch
capabilities.note: Not a denylist and not a permission prompt you click through blind. A command is 'read' only if argv[0] is on a fixed list of readers, no character in it can chain or redirect, and every path argument resolves inside the workspace. git diff/show are excluded because they can execute repo code (textconv). Anything unrecognised falls to 'act', which asks — so the failure mode is a prompt, not a run.

capabilities.name: Talk to it and have it read replies back
evidence: public/index.html: createSpeechOut() reads completed answers and reminders with a localService=true SpeechSynthesisVoice; speakToggle is opt-in
public/index.html: speechChunks() preserves long replies and stop()/generation invalidates cancelled utterances; the speech-out block makes no network call
desktop/Companion.cs: System.Speech SpeechSynthesizer reads results back, with local wake/dictation recognition on Windows
src/voice.js: optional OpenAI-compatible Whisper adapter for recorded audio
src/server.js: /api/transcribe keeps audio uploads behind the existing host, origin, key and MIME guards
test/voice-reply.test.js: the whole panel module boots with a fake DOM and speech synthesis; replies are spoken, remote voices are refused, long replies are chunked and off cancels
docs/VOICE.md: reproduction commands, the offline boundary and what is not claimed
public/visualizer.js: five-state Canvas 2D engine with signal provenance, bounded motion and reduced-motion support
public/audio-input.js: opt-in local microphone FFT/RMS analysis with abort, mute and device-ended cleanup; not speech recognition
test/visualizer.test.js: canonical states, signal freshness, native scalar semantics and renderer lifecycle
test/audio-input.test.js: permission denial, abort/races, device loss and capture cleanup
scripts/test-visualizer-browser.py: synthetic-device Web Audio, reduced motion, keyboard controls and static fallback
capabilities.note: Web dictation uses browser SpeechRecognition, which may send microphone audio to the browser vendor; the Windows companion keeps recognition and TTS on the device with System.Speech. Web spoken replies are opt-in per device, use only voices with localService=true, and need no WHISPER_URL, server TTS endpoint or cloud account. Telegram voice notes still need WHISPER_URL; chat channels get text, not audio replies. Long replies are capped and chunked; devices with no installed local voice stay silent rather than using a network voice. See docs/VOICE.md. Fluid Motion at /visualizer.html analyzes opt-in microphone input locally but does not transcribe it. Conversation/deck visuals consume existing state; native speaking has no output FFT and is labelled decorative. See docs/VISUALIZER.md.

capabilities.name: Shows where an answer came from
evidence: src/sources.js: a per-turn registry — only what this turn actually retrieved can be cited
src/citations.js: citedIds() / validateCitations() — [1], [1,3] and [1-3], checked against the registry

test/citations.test.js: 'the guard flags a citation to something this turn never fetched'

capabilities.note: Validated, not decorative. Every citation is checked against the list of things the turn actually fetched, and a citation that names nothing becomes a visible guard flag rather than a dead link. Sources come from web search, files read, and attachments — not from the model's memory. What this does NOT do: verify that a source supports the sentence it is attached to. That is a semantic judgement, and a code-level check that claims to make it would be lying.

evidence: pinch-tools.example.json: a JSON manifest entry is a tool — name, description, command, args
src/tools.js: loadLocalTools() loads owner-reviewed QUASNOOZE_TOOLS_DIR .js/.mjs modules via registerTool(), refuses collisions and workspace directories, defaults dangerous:true

test/tools.test.js: module loading, trust defaults, approval/denial/unattended refusal and workspace/symlink restrictions

test/custom-tools.test.js: 'a model-supplied argument is data, never a shell' — the semicolon test
docs/GUIDE.md: 'Your own tools (no code required)' — the five guards and what is not supported
capabilities.note: Four extension paths: owner-reviewed local JavaScript modules (QUASNOOZE_TOOLS_DIR; not sandboxed), a JSON manifest for a command you already run (src/custom-tools.js), an MCP server for someone else's tools (src/mcp.js), and a built-in for contributors. Manifest tools are always behind the approval gate — there is no trusted-server opt-out, because the arguments come from the model rather than from code you can read first.

capabilities.name: An agent that runs a task on a schedule without you
evidence: src/schedules.js: parseCadence() accepts `every 30m`, `daily at 09:00`, `weekly on mon at 8:00` — nothing else parses
src/scheduler.js: runSchedules() — a due schedule is a full agent turn, delivered back to the chat that created it
src/agent.js: runAgent({autonomy:'unattended'}) refuses every dangerous tool before the approval gate
test/schedules.test.js: 'an unattended turn refuses a dangerous tool and leaves no approval pending'
docs/GUIDE.md: the 'Tasks that run without you' section
capabilities.note: No catch-up: a schedule missed while the machine was asleep runs once, late, not N times. Interval cadences are measured from the last run, daily/weekly resolve in the owner's timezone, minimum interval 5 minutes, at most 20 schedules. An unattended turn can never approve anything — dangerous tools are refused and the refusal is in the transcript — and it cannot create further schedules, so a loop cannot spawn loops. QUASNOOZE_SCHEDULED_RUNS=0 stops all of it.

capabilities.name: Searches saved conversations across sessions

docs/GUIDE.md: Search past conversations
capabilities.note: Searches retained user/assistant text only, not deleted turns, tool output or system prompts. Sessions retain at most 200 messages; files over 2 MiB or unreadable/malformed files are skipped. No external dependency or persistent search index. All saved sessions share the existing single-owner trust boundary.
